narration_timeline.text: Why do mute swans seem to glide without effort, even when the water around them moves?
narration_timeline.scene: Mute swan visible on a park waterway.

narration_timeline.text: Their bodies float high while webbed feet paddle below the surface, mostly out of sight.
narration_timeline.scene: Mute swan swimming across a quiet pond.

narration_timeline.text: Around ponds and park lakes, some swans swim near other birds, while others stay close to a nest.
narration_timeline.scene: Swan at park lake followed by swan near its nest.

narration_timeline.text: A gentle turn changes the ripples, and the long neck stays balanced above the water.
narration_timeline.scene: Two distinct swan videos at river and park pond.

narration_timeline.text: White feathers make a swan stand out against darker water, even from a distance.
The quiet glide is not magic: small strokes under the surface keep the bird moving forward.
